rule: A crossed bound is a failed check, recorded in followup-failed-legs.json and left failing; only Carl resets one. The old legs C1b, C4 and D3 stay failing and labelled in failed-legs.json with bit-identical results: every new option is opt-in with the old behaviour as its default, and the first validator's output must equal its pinned results byte for byte in measured numbers. No bound moves and no committed threshold is re-read after a result; the alternative is recorded as a question for Carl. A leg that cannot be measured (fewer worlds in a class than the stated minimum) fails by the rule 'a threshold that proves unmeasurable fails the gate on that threshold'. A leg that needs a file is NOT RUN and nothing is fetched. No published number, constant, cluster value or licence term is typed from memory; every world is the first gate's labelled SYNTHETIC world, round numbers, claims about nothing. No background-corrected dispersion is built (Carl, 2026-11-06). The analytic interval stays the default and the bootstrap a labelled option; the Gaussian truncation correction stays on by default with the raw dispersion reported beside it; the tree's rounded SOLAR_MASS_KG is kept for every displayed figure and its relative difference from astropy's solar mass is stated wherever such a figure is stated (reported in R2 of the first gate). An amendment is recorded in this file before any run it concerns, with its reason and the statement that no bound moved.

analysisRule.R16: The distance term of the light. The cluster's redshift z_c is the mean of its members' redshifts and has the statistical error sigma_zc = sd(z of the members) / sqrt(n) (sample standard deviation, n - 1). The luminosity of a galaxy of fixed apparent magnitude goes as D_L(z_c)^2, so the relative error of the cluster's light from the cluster's redshift is 2 (d ln D_L / dz) sigma_zc. In a flat cosmology D_L = (1 + z) D_C and dD_C/dz = (c / H0) / E(z), so d ln D_L / dz = 1/(1 + z) + (c / H0) / (E(z) D_C(z)) (closed form, no differencing). The term is added in quadrature to the photometric term (and before any missing-light share). It is opt-in (light.distanceTerm true; the default false leaves the first gate's light interval bit-identical) and carries the cluster redshift's statistical error only: the cluster's own peculiar velocity, the loss of the true members the clip removes, and the scatter of the selection at the limiting magnitude are not in it and are stated.
analysisRule.R17: The contamination flag on the dispersion's expected bias. Let N_b be the expected number of field galaxies inside the clip window (rule R9 of the first gate: the density outside the window times its width, from velocityExtentKms) and n the members kept (the contaminants included). Field galaxies inside the window are spread over it, a uniform component of half-width w = kappa s and variance w^2 / 3, while the cluster's variance is about s^2; the variance of the kept set is raised by (N_b / n)(w^2 / 3 - s^2), so the fractional bias of the dispersion is, to first order, b = (1/2)(N_b / n)(kappa^2 / 3 - 1), which for kappa = 3 is N_b / n. The flag 'contaminated-bias' is raised when b exceeds one half of the dispersion's own analytic relative error, 1 / (2 sqrt(2 (n - 1))) (the stated reason: a bias of half a standard error lowers the one-sigma coverage of the interval from 0.683 to 0.625, the point where the claimed interval stops being the interval). The rule is opt-in (contaminationRule 'bias'; the default 'share' is the first gate's, so D3 and every old result are bit-identical); the expected bias is reported with every result either way. It is an estimate of the bias, used to flag, and is never subtracted.
analysisRule.R18: The overdensity test for a field with no cluster. After the clip, let n_in be the members, n_pre the galaxies of the pre-selection inside the velocity extent, w the window half-width kappa s and E the extent velocityExtentKms. A field that is uniform in velocity over the extent puts mu = n_pre min(1, w / E) galaxies in the window. The cluster is refused ('not-constrained', code 'no-overdensity') when the exact Poisson upper tail P(X >= n_in | mu) exceeds p_max = 0.001 (the stated reason: a one-in-a-thousand false cluster per field; the window is chosen after the fact to fit the galaxies, which makes the test lenient, and that is stated). Without velocityExtentKms the test is 'unknown' and not applied. It is opt-in (requireOverdensity true; the default false answers a field as the first gate's R6 did).
analysisRule.R19: Defaults kept: the analytic interval is the default dispersion uncertainty and the bootstrap is the labelled option (C1b stays failing and labelled); the Gaussian truncation correction is on with the raw dispersion reported beside it; the displayed solar mass is the tree's SOLAR_MASS_KG, 3.0e-4 above astropy's (R2 of the first gate). No background-corrected dispersion exists in this PR.

checks.what: d ln D_L / dz written in the leg from the cosmology kernel's E(z) and comoving distance, 1/(1+z) + (c/H0)/(E D_C), equals the kernel's to a relative 1e-12 for z in {0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 0.3} and equals a central difference of ln D_L (step 1e-5 z) to a relative 1e-6; the light's relative error with the distance term equals sqrt(photometric^2 + (2 d ln D_L/dz sigma_zc)^2) written in the leg for three members and a stated sigma_zc, to 1e-12; with the option off the result is bit-identical to the first gate's (relSigma equal exactly); sigma_zc equals sd(z)/sqrt(n) for a stated list to 1e-12

the expected fractional bias equals (1/2)(N_b/n)(kappa^2/3 - 1) written in the leg for (N_b, n, kappa) in {(0, 50, 3), (5, 100, 3), (20, 100, 3), (10, 80, 4)} to 1e-12, equals N_b/n at kappa 3; the flag threshold equals 1/(2 sqrt(2(n-1))) for n in {20, 50, 400} to 1e-12; the flag is raised at b just above and not just below it; the default rule 'share' flags exactly as the first gate's (a world with share 0.12 flagged, 0.08 not)

the Poisson upper tail P(X >= n | mu) written in the leg as 1 - sum_{k<n} e^-mu mu^k / k! equals the kernel's for (n, mu) in {(3, 1), (5, 2), (10, 4), (30, 20), (1, 0.5)} to 1e-12 absolute; the test refuses with code 'no-overdensity' when the tail exceeds 0.001 and accepts below it for stated (n_in, n_pre, w, E) cases; mu = n_pre min(1, w/E); without an extent the result is 'unknown' and nothing is refused; with the option off a field is answered

the independent oracle (tools/clusters-oracle/oracle-followup.py: scipy poisson.sf, astropy luminosity distance with a central difference) agrees with the kernel for d ln D_L / dz at 12 redshifts in [0.01, 0.4] to a relative 1e-6 and for the Poisson tail at 20 (n, mu) pairs to 1e-10 absolute

200 light worlds (seed clusters-C4b, the first gate's light row) analysed with light.distanceTerm true: the light interval covers the truth set's sum in [0.563, 0.803] at 0.6827 and [0.89, 0.99] at 0.95. Rule for the bands: the same three binomial standard deviations of 200 worlds about those levels, the upper end capped at 0.99, as the first gate's C4, because the claim is the same claim and only the interval's content changed

600 ladder worlds (seed clusters-D3b), each analysed with contaminationRule 'bias' and velocityExtentKms: (a) calibration: for the interloper fractions 0.1, 0.2 and 0.5 (100 worlds each, at least 80 answered each) the mean estimated expected bias over the answered worlds is within a factor of two of the mean realized fractional bias (sigma_hat - sigma)/sigma, ratio in [0.5, 2] (the rule: R17 is a first-order estimate that ignores the clip's feedback, so only the order is claimed); (b) power and false flags by true bias: with b_true = (1/2)(N_in/(N_m + N_in))(9/3 - 1) from the truth manifest and s_rel = 1/sqrt(2(n_true - 1)), a world is 'clearly biased' when b_true >= 1.0 s_rel and 'clearly fine' when b_true <= 0.25 s_rel; the flag 'contaminated-bias' is raised in at least 90 percent of the answered clearly biased worlds and in at most 10 percent of the answered clearly fine worlds; each class holds at least 50 answered worlds (else the leg fails as unmeasurable)

with requireOverdensity true and velocityExtentKms given: 100 field worlds (seed clusters-R6b-field) are refused 'no-overdensity' in at least 95 of 100; 400 clean ensemble worlds (seed clusters-R6b-clean, 2 percent interlopers) are answered in at least 99 percent (false refusals at most 1 percent); the same field worlds without the option are answered as the first gate's R6 did (the count answered equals 100)

verdictFunction.what: the follow-up kernel verdict, a function of the rows alone: A when A15 to A17, B6, C4b, D3b and R6b all pass; B when A15 to A17 and B6 pass but C4b, D3b or R6b fails (the closed forms of the new terms are claimable, the new intervals or flags are not); C when any of A15 to A17 or B6 fails. It does not change the first gate's kernel verdict B (verdict function in thresholds.json), whose legs stay as recorded; the consumers clause stays unmet whatever this verdict is (Carl, 2026-11-06, question 1).
